title: Require retrieval for refund-policy questions without over-applying

problem.summary: A policy-sensitive refund question was answered without retrieval, producing unsupported guidance.

evidence.observed: The agent answered a refund-eligibility question after the planner span and final-answer span, with no retrieval span in between.

hypothesis.summary: The retrieval policy only keys off explicit source requests, so policy-sensitive refund questions can skip retrieval unless the user asks for sources.
hypothesis.limits: This proposal covers refund-policy behavior only. It does not prove the same routing issue exists for all policy domains.

target.description: Rules that decide when support questions require retrieval before final answer generation.

proposed_change.summary: Require retrieval when a user asks for refund eligibility, exceptions, credits, or cancellation policy, while preserving no-retrieval behavior for simple greetings and account-navigation turns.

require_retrieval_when: input asks whether a user is eligible for a refund, credit, or cancellation exception
input asks what policy applies to a refund or cancellation scenario
answer would make a policy-sensitive recommendation
do_not_force_retrieval_when: input asks how to find the refund page without asking for eligibility
input is already answered by the current authenticated account state

acceptance_criteria.description: Candidate retrieves policy context before answering refund-policy eligibility questions.
Candidate does not force retrieval on simple non-policy turns where retrieval is unnecessary.
Candidate introduces no pass-to-fail verdict flips on guardrail-tagged replay cases.
Candidate stays within latency and retrieval-cost guardrails on unchanged traffic.

risk.notes: The change can increase retrieval calls on borderline refund-related traffic and may add latency or cost if the trigger over-applies.

rollback.plan: Revert the retrieval-policy rule if any guardrail case flips pass-to-fail, p99 retrieval latency exceeds 2200 ms for 24 hours, or daily retrieval cost increases by more than 12% on unchanged traffic.
